target.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users interacting with agents through external chats such as WhatsApp could see automatic runtime notices when model fallback, usage limits, compaction, backend failures, heartbeat checks, ACP status, plugin-binding failures, or tool/progress warnings happened.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds `messages.operationalReplies` so operators can control automatic operational notices separately from normal assistant replies. The policy supports `always`, `silent`, `once`, and `redirect`; `redirect` writes notices to an operator session through `redirectSessionKey`, and `sendPolicy: deny` still wins.

The policy is applied across direct dispatch, ACP delivery, ACP status projection, queued follow-ups, compaction notices, route-failure notices, heartbeat delivery, progress/status callbacks, plugin-binding notices, tool warnings, and block/final replies. Normal message-tool replies, authorized command replies, before-run block replies, and background ACP child suppression keep their existing behavior.

The branch was rebased on current `origin/main`. Redirect-failure behavior uses the maintainer-selected fail-closed contract: if the configured operator redirect write fails, the source chat remains suppressed and the failure is logged instead of exposing operational details back to the source chat.

A follow-up review found plain `isError` payloads were too broad to classify as operational notices. This branch now treats only explicit notice flags or internal notice metadata as operational, and it keeps normal error replies visible under `messages.operationalReplies`.

AI-assisted: yes, Codex helped update this branch and evidence.

## User Impact

Operators can keep fallback, usage-limit, backend-error, compaction, heartbeat, status, ACP, follow-up, plugin-binding, and tool-warning notices out of external chats while still preserving logs or redirecting those notices to an operator-owned session. Existing configs keep current behavior because the default policy is `always`.

## Evidence

Current head: `c248dd95220a66847e2be39f83b434cff57d1f27`

### Real Behavior Proof: WhatsApp-like Source Chat

Earlier redacted terminal proof on this branch used the actual `applyOperationalReplyPolicy` helper, a real temp `sessions.json`, and a source context shaped like an external WhatsApp direct chat:

- source channel: `whatsapp`
- source session: `agent:main:whatsapp:direct:redacted-user`
- payload: `isError: true`, `isFallbackNotice: true`, text `model fallback failed; usage limit reached`

Observed output:

```text
silent: shouldDeliverToSourceChat=false, intentionalSilence=true, externalSends=0, opsTranscriptBytes=0
redirect: shouldDeliverToSourceChat=false, redirected=true, externalSends=0, opsTranscriptHasSourceSession=true, opsTranscriptHasSourceChannel=true, opsTranscriptHasNoticeText=true
redirect transcript excerpt: sourceSessionKey: agent:main:whatsapp:direct:redacted-user | sourceChannel: whatsapp | kind: error
```

This proves the affected external-source path does not deliver the operational fallback/error notice back to the source chat under `silent`, and under `redirect` it keeps source chat sends at zero while writing the notice, source session, source channel, and notice kind into the configured operator session transcript.

### Local Validation

Latest validation after rebasing on current `origin/main`:

- `node scripts/check-session-accessor-boundary.mjs` — passed
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check` — passed
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --write` — refreshed the Plugin SDK hash after `main` moved
- `node --max-old-space-size=8192 --import tsx scripts/generate-plugin-sdk-api-baseline.ts --check` — passed
- `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_DIR=extensions node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.auto-reply-reply.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/acp-projector.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/followup-runner.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.misc.runreplyagent.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-acp-delivery.test.ts` — 5 files, 580 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts test/scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.test.ts` — 1 file, 9 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
